rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated formula of denying the messengers will introduce parallel accounts of the people of Ad, Thamud, Lot, and the Thicket.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي حكاية تكذيب عاد وثمود وقوم لوط وأصحاب ليكة على هذا النمط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is a temporal adverb: they denied Noah when he said ألا تتقون, and answered with their objection about his low-status followers.
rows.anchor: أي كذبوه حين قال لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah had likely called them repeatedly before this admonition, which came when he saw them persist in disbelief; their reply about the lowly followers supports this.
rows.anchor: صدر بعد أن دعاهم من قبل وكرر دعوتهم إذ رآهم مصرين على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra selects this episode from Noah’s career because its parallel with Muhammad’s situation consoles the Prophet.
rows.anchor: هذا الموقف من مواقفه لأنه أنسب بغرض السورة في تسلية الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here brother means a kinsman belonging to the same tribe.
rows.anchor: والأخ مستعمل في معنى القريب من القبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes ألا as interrogative hamza plus negative لا; the question denies their piety and implies refusal to comply with Noah’s call.
rows.anchor: مركبا من حرفين همزة استفهام دخلت على ( لا ) النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ألا is a single exhortative particle, implying that they are slow to believe Noah.
rows.anchor: حرفا واحدا هو حرف التحضيض مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety here means fearing God’s punishment for associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: خشية الله من عقابه إياهم على أن جعلوا معه شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s claim to be a trusted messenger explains his rebuke or exhortation: they persist in polytheism despite his prohibition, although he is their trustworthy messenger.
rows.anchor: تعليل للإنكار أو للتحضيض ، أي كيف تستمرون على الشرك وقد نهيتكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was known and trusted by his people before his mission, just as Muhammad was called al-Amīn among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: نوح موسوما بالأمانة لا يتهم في قومه كما كان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s poetic line presents Noah as one who does not betray trust.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : كذلك كان نوح لا يخون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إني anticipates that they may challenge Noah’s trustworthiness; his prior record of honesty supports the truth of his message and indirectly rebukes Quraysh for denying Muhammad after calling him trustworthy.
rows.anchor: وتأكيده بحرف التأكيد مع عدم سبق إنكارهم أمانته لأنه توقع حدوث الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible sense of أمين is that Noah was entrusted by God with the community to which he was sent.
rows.anchor: أن يراد به أمين من جانب الله على الأمة التي أرسل إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-wage statement is joined to Noah’s declaration of trustworthiness: they know he is honest and seeks no personal benefit from calling them to faith.
rows.anchor: أي علمتم أني أمين لكم وتعلمون أني لا أطلب من دعوتكم إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun عليه refers to the understood matter of Noah’s invitation.
rows.anchor: عائد إلى معلوم من مقام الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command reiterates ألا تتقون and interrupts two coordinated clauses; Noah repeats the call after its explanation, after saying he seeks no wage, and again as the speech’s conclusion.
rows.anchor: وهو اعتراض بين الجملتين المتعاطفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ of the first-person suffix is omitted from أطيعون in both occurrences, as in 26:14.
rows.anchor: في الموضعين كما حذفت في قوله

words: إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Noah’s reward rests only with the Lord alludes to the Day of Recompense, which his people denied.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى يوم الجزاء وكانوا ينكرون البعث كما دل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers readers to the earlier mention of Noah among those God chose.
rows.anchor: وتقدم ذكر نوح عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قالوا is an explanatory resumption answering the listener’s curiosity about the exchange prompted by the account of Noah’s people denying the messengers; قالوا and قال present the debate.
rows.anchor: من استشراف السامع لمعرفة ما دار بينهم وبين نوح من حوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers were the chiefs who took charge of debating Noah.
rows.anchor: هم كبراء القوم الذين تصدوا لمحاورة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a denial: they will not believe Noah because the lowly people followed him; واتبعك is a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: أي لا نؤمن لك وقد اتبعك الأرذلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called the poorer and weaker followers contemptible, arrogantly rejecting equality with them in following Noah.
rows.anchor: أرادوا بهم ضعفاء القوم وفقراءهم فتكبروا وتعاظموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh chiefs similarly asked Muhammad to expel believers such as ʿAmmār, Bilāl, and Zayd, promising they might then follow; the verse in al-Anʿām answered them.
rows.anchor: لما كان من المؤمنين عمار وبلال وزيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كانوا is an extra emphatic insertion between relative ما and its clause; the wāw is its subject, not a pronoun of كان, since extra كان does not take a predicate.
rows.anchor: أي تأكيد مدلول ( ما علمي بما يعملون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase covers all their religious and worldly conduct, past, present, and future, outward and inward.
rows.anchor: جميع أحوالهم في دينهم ودنياهم في الماضي والحال والمستقبل والظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥisāb literally means counting; here it means fully examining the apparent and hidden reality of deeds so none is missed or confused.
rows.anchor: استعمل في معنى تمحيض الأعمال وتحقيق ظواهرها وبواطنها بحيث لا يفوت منها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone will deal with their past and present deeds and know their true reality; Noah adds that point as an essential part of his response to their demand to expel believers.
rows.anchor: من شموله جميع أعمالهم الظاهرة والباطنة التي منها ما يحاسبون عليه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that those who profess the testimony of God’s oneness have their blood and property protected except by right, while their true account belongs to God; Ibn ʿĀshūr gives no grading.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( فإذا قالوها ( أي لا إلاه إلا الله ) عصموا مني دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها وحسابهم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is a restriction of the described subject to a predicate: حسابهم is the subject and على ربي its qualifying predicate, in al-Sakkākī’s analysis.
rows.anchor: قصر موصوف على الصفة ، والموصوف هو { حسابهم } والصفة هي { على ربي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is an additional restriction: their account belongs to God rather than Noah, answering the chiefs’ demand to expel believers as supposedly unworthy of equal faith.
rows.anchor: قصر إفراد إضافي ، أي لا يتجاوز الكون على ربي إلى الاتصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لو تشعرون exposes their ignorance and false pride; its omitted result is that they would realize their account belongs to God, not Noah, and would not have made their demand.
rows.anchor: تجهيل لهم ورغم لغرورهم وإعجابهم الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in Hūd explicitly calls them ignorant, supporting this reading; Ibn ʿĀshūr says it fits the verse’s form and meaning without added suppositions.
rows.anchor: هذا هو التفسير الذي يطابق نظم الآية ومعناها من غير احتياج إلى زيادات وفروض

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Other commentators take الأرذلون to mean people of genuinely base status, thereby treating the question as a challenge to the sincerity of Noah’s converts.
rows.anchor: المفسرون نحوا منحى تأويل الأرذلون } أنهم الموصوفون بالرذالة الدنية

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Those commentators read Noah as disclaiming any ability to inspect the followers’ inner states and sincerity, taking their account as the reckoning at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: تبرؤا من الكشف على ضمائرهم وصحة إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr finds that interpretation unsatisfying: it appears to have been driven by reading حساب as the final Judgment, which does not fit the passage as well.
rows.anchor: فحملوه على الحساب الذي يقع يوم الجزاء وذلك لا يثلج له الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After invalidating the basis for expulsion, Noah explicitly says that he will not drive the believers away.
rows.anchor: فبعد أن أبطل مقتضى طردهم صرح بأنه لا يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s role as a clear warner explains why he cannot comply with the chiefs’ demand.
rows.anchor: استئناف في معنى التعليل ، أي لأن وصفي يصرفني عن موافقتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبين derives from transitive أبان in the sense of making clear and explaining.
rows.anchor: من أبان المتعدي بمعنى بين ووضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is additional and restricts the described subject to a single quality.
rows.anchor: والقصر إضافي وهو قصر موصوف على صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s similar exchange in Hūd may be a separate occasion or the same exchange retold with each Qur’anic account supplying complementary details.
rows.anchor: حكاية موقف لنوح عليه السلام مع قومه شبيه بما حكي هنا وبين الحكايتين اختلاف ما

words: لئن لم تنته يانوح لتكونن من المرجومين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When argument failed, Noah’s opponents resorted to the bullies’ weapon: threatening physical harm.
rows.anchor: صاروا إلى سلاح المبطلين وهو المناضلة بالأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rجم means throwing stones and commonly means killing by stoning; من المرجومين places Noah in a class of people deserving that punishment.
rows.anchor: الرمي بالحجارة ، وقد غلب استعماله في القتل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is like Noah’s words in al-Anʿām, وما أنا من المهتدين, which likewise identifies a person as belonging to a class.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم في قوله : { وما أنا من المهتدين } في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s statement prepares his prayer against his people and expresses grief and despair that they will stop denying him.
rows.anchor: تمهيد للدعاء عليهم وهو خبر مستعمل في إنشاء التحسر واليأس من إقلاعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتح means judgment; its emphatic repetition as فتحا asks for a severe judgment, namely annihilation, while the following request safeguards Noah and the believers from it.
rows.anchor: الحكم ، وتأكيده ب { فتحا } لإرادة حكم شديد ، وهو الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المشحون means filled.
rows.anchor: و { المشحون } : المملوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثم marks rank rather than elapsed time: drowning an entire people is a greater sign of power than rescuing a small group.
rows.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي في الإخبار لأن إغراق أمة كاملة أعظم دلالة على عظيم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from كذبون for the verse ending, as in 26:14.
rows.anchor: للفاصلة كما تقدم في قوله : { فأخاف أن يقتلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resumes the consoling accounts for the Prophet and the repeated admonition of deniers after the account of Noah’s people.
rows.anchor: استئناف تعداد لأخبار التسلية للرسول وتكرير الموعظة للمكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means Ad denied Hud and also denied Noah’s message, since Hud reminded them of Noah’s people’s fate.
rows.anchor: يفيد أنهم كذبوا رسولهم هودا وكذبوا رسالة نوح لأن هودا وعظهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine tāʾ in كذبت agrees with ʿĀd understood as the name of a nation.
rows.anchor: لان اسم عاد علم على أمة فهو مؤول بمعنى الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of ألا تتقون is the same as in the parallel opening of Noah’s story.
rows.anchor: مثل القول في نظيره المتقدم في قصة قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud, like Noah, was known for trustworthiness and good character before his mission; their claim that a god had afflicted him implies a change from his former state.
rows.anchor: فإن الرسول لا يبعث إلا وقد كان معروفا بالأمانة وحسن الخلق قبل الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud’s command follows from his appeal just as it does in Noah’s story; the yāʾ of أطيعون is omitted for the verse ending, as in Noah’s and Abraham’s accounts.
rows.anchor: عليه كما تقدم في قصة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier account of ʿĀd and Hud is found at the cited passage in al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وتقدم ذكر عاد وهود عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordinated clause remains within the scope of the preceding reproach and shares its circumstantial qualification; many legal theorists allow an intervening circumstantial clause to govern both when context supports it.
rows.anchor: بناء على أن الحال المتوسطة بين الجملتين ترجع إلى كلتيهما على رأي كثير من علماء أصول الفقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ over the buildings, signs, and factories: some interpret them as sheer frivolity and corruption, others as originally permissible, and others as useful works.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض ما قالوه ما هو متمحض للهو والعبث والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is an inclusion substitution explaining ألا تتقون: building in this way is one of the acts encompassed by the denied lack of piety.
rows.anchor: فإن مضمونها مما يشتمل عليه عدم التقوى الذي تسلط عليه الإنكار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains الريع as an elevated place.
rows.anchor: الشرف ، أي المكان المرتفع ، كذا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda explain الريع as a road or a pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: والطريق والفج بين الجبلين ، كذا قال مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An āya is a marker that guides a traveler, and it can also mean an impressive construction that signals its maker’s skill or its owner’s grandeur.
rows.anchor: والآية : العلامة الدالة على الطريق ، وتطلق الآية على المصنوع المعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كل is used to indicate abundance: the elevated sites overlooking the traveled roads.
rows.anchor: و ( كل ) مستعمل في الكثرة ، أي في الأرياع المشرفة على الطرق المسلوكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبث is an act that yields no useful benefit.
rows.anchor: العمل الذي لا فائدة نفع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مصانع is the plural of مصنع, derived from صنع on the mafʿal pattern; it is a verbal noun used adjectivally for emphasis.
rows.anchor: جمع مصنع وأصله مفعل مشتق من صنع فهو مصدر ميمي وصف به للمبالغة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the factories to be cisterns dug into the ground.
rows.anchor: هو الجابية المحفورة في الأرض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that they were lime-built reservoirs for storing water, called ṣahrīj or mājal.
rows.anchor: وروي عن قتادة : مبنية بالجير يخزن بها الماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the factories were palaces.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قصور وهو عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land of ʿĀd lay between Oman and Hadramawt east to west and extended north to the sands called al-Aḥqāf.
rows.anchor: بلاد عاد ما بين عمان وحضرموت شرقا وغربا ومتغلغلة في الشمال إلى الرمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لعل introduces a wish, but the claim that their buildings might make them immortal is sarcastic.
rows.anchor: و ( لعل ) للترجي ، وهو طلب المتكلم شيئا مستقرب الحصول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says ʿĀd built on high points along roads to amuse themselves and mock passersby; Ibn ʿĀshūr explains this as turning useful public works into corrupt diversions in a declining society.
rows.anchor: جعلت عاد بنايات على المرتفعات على الطرق يعبثون فيها ويسخرون بالمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the conversion of useful places to vice with Arab monasteries used as drinking halls and Carthage cisterns, once water stores, later used by thieves and animals until 1303 AH.
rows.anchor: كما اتخذت بعض أديرة النصارى في بلاد العرب مجالس خمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God follows the reproach about their buildings and harshness when angry, and the command to obey Hud is repeated with it.
rows.anchor: فرع عليه أمرهم باتقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ of the first-person suffix is omitted from أطيعون, as in the parallel occurrence.
rows.anchor: وحذف ياء المتكلم من { أطيعون } كحذفها في نظيرها المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the syntax could have been فاتقوا الله الذي أمدكم, the second imperative repeats اتقوا to emphasize piety and restore the flow after وأطيعون separates the clause.
rows.anchor: وهو مستغنى عنه لو اقتصر على الموصول وصفا لاسم الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command is coordinated because it adds a reminder of God’s beneficence; naming God first points to His intrinsic right to piety, while naming His gifts points to gratitude.
rows.anchor: لما في الجملة الثانية من الزيادة على ما في الجملة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud first gives a general reminder of provision, preparing his listeners for the specific blessings named next.
rows.anchor: ذكر النعمة بالإجمال الذي يهيىء السامعين لتلقي ما يرد بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second أمدكم repeats the first for emphasis; its detailed list is also a partitive apposition specifying some of what the general phrase includes, so the sentence is not coordinated.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة بمنزلة بدل البعض من جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later speech explains the rebuke in ألا تتقون: their current way of life will not last, since they will leave this world and return to God.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنكار عليهم دوام حالهم يقتضي أنهم مفارقون هذه الحياة وصائرون إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation to preserve blessings through gratitude includes the maxim that failing to thank for blessings invites their loss, while gratitude binds them fast.
rows.anchor: حث على العمل لاستبقاء تلك النعم بأن يشكروا الله عليها كما قال صاحب ( الحكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هاهنا points to their land and, by extension, everything they see; this is an eloquent compression.
rows.anchor: و { هاهنا } إشارة إلى بلادهم ، أي في جميع ما تشاهدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آمنين explains part of the general reference to what is here: it draws attention to the great, unseen blessing of security, without which other blessings cannot be enjoyed.
rows.anchor: وذلك تنبيه على نعمة عظيمة لا يدل عليها اسم الإشارة لأنها لا يشار إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في جنات should attach to آمنين, together specifying their security and abundant comfort as details of the general reference.
rows.anchor: أي اجتمع لهم الأمن ورفاهية العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are walled orchards planted with date palms and grapevines.
rows.anchor: الحوائط التي تشجر بالنخيل والأعناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṭalʿ is the palm’s early fruit case, sword-tip shaped with the cluster inside; called kumm, it splits after days to expose the branches of small fruit, which thicken and become dates.
rows.anchor: فيه ثمر النخلة في أول أطواره يخرج كنصل السيف في باطنه شماريخ القنو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هضيم means softened or crushed; by metaphor it describes slender, delicate fruiting growth and indicates that the palms yield good dates.
rows.anchor: بمعنى المهضوم ، وأصل الهضم شدخ الشيء حتى يلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palms yielding good dates are called female palms; the opposite are male palms, whose clusters and dates are thick.
rows.anchor: بضم الفاء وتشديد الحاء المهملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palms are singled out although already included in the gardens, to emphasize their quality through the fine fruiting growth.
rows.anchor: مع أنه مما تشمله الجنات لقصد بيان جودته بأن طلعه هضيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وتنحتون is coordinated with آمنين, meaning that they are also carvers; the present tense vividly depicts their carving houses from mountains.
rows.anchor: عبر عنه بصيغة المضارع لاستحضار الحالة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads فرهين without an alif after fāʾ, as an intensive form from فراهة, meaning skill and cleverness.
rows.anchor: و { فرهين } صيغة مبالغة في قراءة الجمهور بدون ألف بعد الفاء ، مشتق من الفراهة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read فارهين as an active participle.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف { فارهين } بصيغة اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word describes skilled carvers whose mountain homes look as if they were built.
rows.anchor: أي عارفين حذقين بنحت البيوت من الجبال بحيث تصير بالنحت كأنها مبنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God and obey the messenger follows from the preceding rebuke as in the story of Hud.
rows.anchor: مفرع مثل نظيره في قصة عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The المسرفين are the people’s leaders, who lure them into idol worship and exploit their ignorance for their own benefit.
rows.anchor: أيمة القوم وكبراؤهم الذين يغرونهم بعبادة الأصنام ويبقونهم في الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إسراف is excess; here it includes all blameworthy excess in wealth and disbelief, and is tied to corruption.
rows.anchor: الإفراط في شيء ، والمراد به هنا الإسراف المذموم كله في المال وفي الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their excess is characterized as corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: ووصفهم بأنهم { يفسدون في الأرض } ، فالإسراف منوط بالفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordinating the denial of reform confirms their corruption by negating its opposite; the parallel wording in Ṭā Hā illustrates this reinforcement.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لوقوع الشيء بنفي ضده مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: عمرو بن مرة الجهني
rows.claim: The poetic phrase النسب المعروف غير المنكر is cited as evidence for reinforcing a statement by denying its opposite.
rows.anchor: وقول عمرو بن مرة الجهني : النسب المعروف غير المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating reform shows that no goodness mixes with their corruption; this confirms the charge without using an exclusive construction that could be dismissed as hyperbole.
rows.anchor: يفيد أن فسادهم لا يشوبه صلاح ؛ فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: السموأل أو الحارثي
rows.claim: A line attributed uncertainly to al-Samawʾal or al-Ḥārithī illustrates affirming one thing by denying its opposite.
rows.anchor: كقول السموأل أو الحارثي : تسيل على حد الظبات نفوسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in الأرض refers to an already known earth.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { الأرض } تعريف العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer his warning with slander, claiming that he has lost his reason and changed because of powerful sorcery.
rows.anchor: أجابوا موعظته بالبهتان فزعموه فقد رشده وتغير حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المسحر is one subjected to powerful sorcery; من المسحرين is more emphatic than simply calling him مسحر, as in 26:116.
rows.anchor: فالمسحر : اسم مفعول سحره إذا سحره سحرا متمكنا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reinforce their denial by arguing that a human like them cannot be a messenger; they imagined a messenger must be a supernatural creature such as an angel or jinn.
rows.anchor: أيدوا تكذيبه بأنه بشر مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that Ṣāliḥ is merely human functions as a reinforcing confirmation of the claim that he is bewitched.
rows.anchor: في حكم التأكيد بجملة : { إنما أنت من المسحرين } باعتبار مضمون الجملتين

words: لئن لم تنته يالوط لتكونن من المخرجين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like Noah’s people, Lot’s opponents threaten him, but they threaten expulsion because he was an immigrant from outside the town who had married into the community.
rows.anchor: فهددوه بالإخراج من مدينتهم لأنه كان من غير أهل المدينة بل كان مهاجرا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction من المخرجين is more emphatic than saying لنخرجنك, as with من المرجومين in Noah’s story.
rows.anchor: وصيغة { من المخرجين } أبلغ من : لنخرجنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s reply dismisses their threat: he says that he detests their deed.
rows.anchor: جواب مستخف بوعيدهم إذ أعاد الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من القالين is more emphatic than simply saying he hates their deed, and creates a complete, extended paronomasia between قال and القالين.
rows.anchor: أبلغ في الوصف من أن يقول : إني لعملكم قالل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is glossed as meaning one of those who hate or detest the deed.
rows.anchor: أي من المبغضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot asks to be saved from the punishment for their deeds, with punishment understood; reading it as asking not to commit their deed loses the allusion to what will befall them.
rows.anchor: أي من عذاب ما يعملونه فلا بد من تقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Lot and his people has already appeared in al-Aʿrāf, Hūd, and al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: والقصة تقدمت في الأعراف وفي هود والحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence: Lot’s rescue followed his prayer after only the short interval before God ordered him to leave with his family for Ṣughar.
rows.anchor: للتعقيب ، أي كانت نجاته عقب دعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The old woman is Lot’s elderly wife.
rows.anchor: المرأة المسنة وهي زوج لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في الغابرين qualifies عجوزا; the wife is excluded from Lot’s rescued family and remained in the punishment after they left.
rows.anchor: والغابر : المتصف بالغبور وهو البقاء بعد ذهاب الأصحاب
